variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Construct SFT data as an auditable dataset”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Collect representative failures
pairs.detail: Sample real task shapes and edge cases.
pairs.explanation: Sample real task shapes and edge cases. Preserve source, permission, language, tenant, time, and difficulty metadata.

pairs.label: Write canonical responses
pairs.explanation: Use the production output contract. Review factual support, policy behavior, tool arguments, and ambiguous cases.

pairs.label: Deduplicate and group
pairs.detail: Cluster exact and near duplicates before splitting.
pairs.explanation: Cluster exact and near duplicates before splitting. Keep the same user, source document, conversation, or incident in one split group.

pairs.label: Freeze train, validation, and test
pairs.detail: Use validation for checkpoint and hyperparameter choices.
pairs.explanation: Use validation for checkpoint and hyperparameter choices. Keep the final test set untouched until the release candidate is selected.

variants.title: Make the decision
variants.context: Fine-tuning updates some or all parameters of a pretrained model so it performs a defined task more consistently. In supervised fine-tuning (SFT), each training record demonstrates the input the application will send and the output the model should produce.
variants.prompt: A model answers from policies that change every week. What should the first production baseline usually test?
options: Full-parameter fine-tuning on last month's policy text
Retrieval with current sources, citation checks, and a prompt baseline
More epochs on the existing dataset
A larger LoRA rank without a held-out set
variants.explanation: Frequently changing facts belong in a versioned retrieval path first. Fine-tuning can shape behavior, but it does not keep facts current by itself.
optionFeedback: Frequently changing facts belong in a versioned retrieval path first. Fine-tuning can shape behavior, but it does not keep facts current by itself.

variants.hint: Think about the key idea first: In plain language: prompting tells a model what to do in one request; retrieval gives it current evidence; fine-tuning lets it practice a stable behavior across many examples.

When facts change hourly and no retrieval system exists
When the task rubric has not been defined

To remove the need for slice metrics
